requirements: Reproduce the nncase end-to-end compilation framework and demonstrate its LLM inference performance advantages on heterogeneous CPU architectures.

sub_tasks.requirements: The evaluation hardware, OS, compiler toolchain, and comparison-framework versions are configured to match the paper.
The physical hardware platform matches the paper's evaluation setup.
Evaluation is performed on an AMD Ryzen 9 5900X 12-core processor (or the closest available equivalent explicitly documented if not accessible).

sub_tasks.requirements: The e-graph-based equality saturation engine, cost model, and WPMAXSAT-based extraction are implemented as the foundational term rewriting infrastructure supporting Auto Vectorize and Auto Distribution modules.
The core e-graph data structure representing e-classes and e-nodes is implemented with correct semantics.

Code has been implemented that defines an EGraph class containing e-classes (equivalence classes) and e-nodes (computation nodes), where each e-node references child e-classes rather than concrete nodes.

verification.spec: Import the EGraph class and instantiate it. Add e-nodes and assert (a) EGraph exposes e-classes and e-nodes as separate collections, (b) each e-node stores its children as e-class ids (not e-node ids) — inspect an e-node's children field and confirm the ids resolve via EGraph.find to e-classes, (c) equivalent e-nodes are grouped under a shared e-class id.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented providing an Add operation that inserts an e-node into the e-graph and returns an e-class identifier.

verification.spec: Construct an empty EGraph, call `eg.Add(node)` for a leaf e-node, assert it returns an integer/handle representing an e-class id, and that calling `eg.find(id)` returns a valid canonical id. Adding a second distinct node returns a different id.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented providing a Union operation that merges two or more e-classes into a single equivalence class using a union-find (disjoint-set) structure.

verification.spec: Create an EGraph, add e-nodes a, b, c yielding three distinct e-classes A, B, C. Call union(A, B) then union(B, C) and assert find(A) == find(B) == find(C). Also assert the underlying data structure is union-find (path-compression / rank-tracking) by inspecting internal parent/rank arrays or by an O(alpha(n)) amortized-time micro-benchmark on 10k unions.

sub_tasks.requirements: The e-graph maintains hash-consing / canonicalization so that structurally identical e-nodes referencing the same child e-classes are deduplicated (adding the same node twice returns the same e-class id).

verification.spec: Add an e-node N with a given op and child e-class ids to the EGraph, obtaining id1. Add a structurally identical e-node N' with the same op and same child e-class ids, obtaining id2. Assert id1 == id2 (hash-consing). Repeat for at least 3 distinct node types.

sub_tasks.requirements: After Union operations, the e-graph is rebuilt/repaired so that all parent e-nodes referencing merged e-classes are re-canonicalized (upward merging propagation is implemented).

verification.spec: Build an e-graph with a parent e-node P referencing child e-classes C1 and C2. Union C1 and C2, then call rebuild(). Assert that (a) P's children are re-canonicalized to point to find(C1)==find(C2), (b) any two parent e-nodes that became structurally identical after the merge are themselves unioned into the same e-class (upward merging propagation), and (c) hashcons/lookup returns the canonical e-class for the merged parents.

sub_tasks.requirements: The equality saturation loop with pattern matching and rewrite rule application is implemented.
Code has been implemented that provides a rewrite rule interface supporting a left-hand-side pattern and a right-hand-side rewritten term, applied non-destructively to the e-graph.

verification.spec: Define a rewrite rule via the public API with an LHS pattern `Add(?a, 0)` and RHS `?a`. Apply it to an e-graph containing Add(x, 0). Assert (1) after application, the e-graph still contains the original Add(x,0) e-node (non-destructive), (2) the e-class of Add(x,0) is now unioned with the e-class of x, and (3) both representations remain extractable.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for an e-matching pattern matcher that finds all e-class substitutions satisfying a rule's LHS pattern in the current e-graph.

verification.spec: Build an e-graph containing multiple matches for pattern `Mul(?a, ?b)`: e.g., Mul(x,y), Mul(y,x), Mul(a,b). Call the e-matcher on this LHS and assert it returns a list of substitutions with correct bindings for ?a and ?b for each match, and that the number of returned substitutions equals the number of Mul e-nodes.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for an equality saturation driver that iteratively (a) collects all pattern matches, (b) applies rewrites by adding new e-nodes and unioning e-classes, (c) rebuilds the e-graph, until saturation or a configurable iteration/node limit is reached.

verification.spec: Instantiate the saturation runner with the Table 1 rewrite rules on the Figure 2(a) input. Assert the runner (a) performs a match phase that returns all pattern hits before any application (no destructive rewriting), (b) applies matches by adding e-nodes and calling union, (c) calls rebuild() at the end of each iteration, (d) terminates when the iteration reports zero new unions/e-nodes (saturation) OR when a configurable node/iteration limit is hit — verify both termination modes by running twice with different limits.

sub_tasks.requirements: The saturation loop applies all applicable rules simultaneously per iteration (breadth-first application) rather than sequentially destroying the IR, preserving all equivalent program versions.

verification.spec: Register two rewrite rules R1 and R2 whose combined effect only produces the optimal outcome when applied in a specific order under greedy rewriting (as illustrated by the transpose example in Fig. 2). Run the saturation loop, then extract the minimum-cost program. Assert (a) the extracted program equals the globally optimal form regardless of rule registration order, and (b) the e-graph contains e-nodes from both intermediate states (evidencing simultaneous, non-destructive application).

sub_tasks.requirements: The transpose-optimization rewrite rules from Table 1 are implemented and demonstrated on the motivating example in Figure 2.
Code implements the CombineBinaryLeftTrans rewrite rule: Binary(Tperm(A), B) -> Tperm(Binary(A, Tperm^{-1}(B))).

verification.spec: Locate the CombineBinaryLeftTrans rule in the source. Build an e-graph with Binary(Tperm(A, perm=[1,0]), B). Run saturation with only this rule enabled and extract. Assert the resulting program contains Tperm(Binary(A, Tperm(B, perm_inv))) where perm_inv equals the inverse permutation. Verify numerically on a concrete tensor pair that both forms compute the same result.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code implements the CombineBinaryRightTrans rewrite rule: Binary(A, Tperm(B)) -> Tperm(Binary(Tperm^{-1}(A), B)).

verification.spec: Locate the CombineBinaryRightTrans rule in the source. Build an e-graph with Binary(A, Tperm(B, perm=[1,0])). Run saturation with only this rule enabled and extract. Assert the resulting program contains Tperm(Binary(Tperm(A, perm_inv), B)). Verify numerically on a concrete tensor pair that both forms compute the same result.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code implements the CombineUnaryTrans rewrite rule: Unary(Tperm(A)) -> Tperm(Unary(A)).

verification.spec: Construct an IR expression Unary(Transpose(A, perm)) and apply the CombineUnaryTrans rewrite rule. Assert the result equals Transpose(Unary(A), perm) structurally, and verify numerical equivalence for a concrete random tensor A and a chosen perm.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code implements the FoldTwoTrans rewrite rule: Tperm2(Tperm1(A)) -> Tperm composed with perm1[perm2[i]] for i in [0, Len(perm2)).

verification.spec: Build Tperm2(Tperm1(A)) with two permutations perm1 and perm2, apply FoldTwoTrans, and assert the result is a single Transpose whose permutation equals perm1 composed with perm2 (i.e., perm1[perm2[i]] for all i). Verify numerically on a random tensor.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code implements the FoldNopTrans rewrite rule: T[0,1,...,n](A) -> A (identity transpose folding).

verification.spec: Construct Transpose(A, [0,1,...,n-1]) (identity permutation) and apply FoldNopTrans. Assert the rewritten expression is exactly A (no transpose node remains). Also verify that non-identity permutations are NOT folded.

sub_tasks.requirements: On the Figure 2(a) example graph, applying equality saturation with the Table 1 rules followed by extraction produces the fully optimized graph shown in Figure 2(f) with all redundant transposes eliminated, matching the optimal path (2b) rather than the suboptimal path (2c).

verification.spec: Construct the Figure 2(a) input graph (Transpose+Binary+Unary composition) programmatically. Run the implemented equality saturation with the five rules from Table 1 (CombineBinaryLeftTrans, CombineBinaryRightTrans, CombineUnaryTrans, FoldTwoTrans, FoldNopTrans), then extract. Assert the extracted graph contains zero Transpose (Tperm) nodes, matching Figure 2(f).

sub_tasks.requirements: A Roofline-based cost model assigns weights to e-nodes for extraction.

Code has been implemented for a Roofline cost model that computes per-e-node cost from memory traffic (bytes accessed) and compute cycles (FLOPs / peak throughput), taking the maximum of the two as the operator's execution time.

verification.spec: Import the roofline cost function and call it on synthetic operators: (a) memory-bound (large tensor copy, few FLOPs) -> assert returned cost == bytes/bandwidth (memory term dominates); (b) compute-bound (small tensor, huge FLOPs) -> assert cost == flops/peak_throughput (compute term dominates); (c) balanced -> assert cost == max(mem_time, compute_time). Verify the function accepts peak_bandwidth and peak_flops as parameters.

sub_tasks.requirements: The cost model accepts hardware parameters (peak compute throughput, memory bandwidth per level) so that costs can be re-targeted to different devices without changing rewrite rules.

verification.spec: Instantiate the Roofline cost model with two distinct hardware descriptors (e.g., differing peak FLOPS and memory bandwidths per memory level) and evaluate the cost of the same e-node. Assert that (a) the API accepts the hardware parameters without modifying rewrite rules, and (b) the returned costs differ consistently with the changed parameters (e.g., halving bandwidth roughly doubles memory-time contribution).

sub_tasks.requirements: The cost model produces per-e-node numeric weights used as objective coefficients when extracting the minimum-cost subgraph.

verification.spec: Build an e-graph with a few nodes of differing costs (e.g., MatMul vs Transpose+MatMul). Call the cost model API on each e-node and assert it returns a numeric (float/int) weight. Then invoke the WPMAXSAT extractor and confirm the objective coefficients passed to the solver equal the cost model outputs (introspect via a debug hook or by monkeypatching the cost function to return known values and checking the resulting extraction).

sub_tasks.requirements: WPMAXSAT-based extraction selects the optimal acyclic subgraph from the saturated e-graph.

Code has been implemented that encodes e-graph extraction as a Weighted Partial MaxSAT (WPMAXSAT) problem, with a boolean variable per e-node indicating whether it is selected in the extracted program.

verification.spec: Import the extraction module and confirm it exposes a function that converts an e-graph into a WPMAXSAT instance. Inspect the returned instance and assert (a) there is exactly one boolean variable per e-node, (b) soft clauses carry the roofline weights, (c) hard clauses encode e-class selection (exactly-one-per-selected-class) constraints.

sub_tasks.requirements: Hard clauses enforce that exactly one e-node is chosen per selected e-class and that if an e-node is chosen, e-nodes representing each of its child e-classes must also be chosen (root reachability).

verification.spec: Construct a small e-graph with an e-class containing two e-nodes and child references. Run extraction and inspect the generated hard clauses (or force by constraint injection): assert exactly one e-node is selected per reachable e-class from the root, and for any selected e-node, at least one e-node in each of its child e-classes is also selected.

sub_tasks.requirements: Acyclic constraints are added so that the extracted subgraph forms a DAG (no e-node depends transitively on itself), following the acyclic-constraint extraction approach.

verification.spec: Construct a small e-graph that admits a cyclic selection (e.g., two e-classes each containing an e-node referencing the other) alongside a valid acyclic alternative. Run the extractor and assert (a) the extractor's SAT encoding includes acyclicity constraints (inspect generated clauses), (b) the returned assignment yields a DAG when traversed, and (c) no e-node in the extracted set depends transitively on itself.

sub_tasks.requirements: Soft clauses encode the per-e-node cost weights from the Roofline cost model so the MaxSAT solver minimizes total extracted cost.

verification.spec: Build an e-graph with two equivalent extraction candidates whose per-e-node Roofline costs differ. Extract and confirm the lower-total-cost candidate is chosen. Then modify one e-node's weight so the alternative becomes cheaper and confirm the extractor now picks the alternative, proving soft clauses encode the cost weights.

sub_tasks.requirements: The extraction dispatches to a MaxSAT solver (e.g., OR-Tools or an equivalent WPMAXSAT backend) and reconstructs the extracted program from the solver's boolean assignment.

verification.spec: Invoke the extraction API on a small e-graph and assert (a) an external MaxSAT/WPMAXSAT solver (e.g., OR-Tools CP-SAT or equivalent) is called (monkey-patch or log to verify), (b) the resulting boolean assignment is parsed back into a chosen e-node per e-class, and (c) the returned program object is a valid IR reconstruction whose root corresponds to the requested root e-class.

sub_tasks.requirements: On a small e-graph containing both the suboptimal (Figure 2c) and optimal (Figure 2b/f) transpose-elimination programs, the WPMAXSAT extractor selects the optimal path with strictly lower total cost.

verification.spec: Build a small e-graph manually containing both the Figure 2(c) suboptimal program (>=1 residual Transpose) and the Figure 2(b/f) optimal program (0 Transpose) as equivalent alternatives. Assign roofline costs so that Transpose has strictly positive cost. Run the WPMAXSAT extractor and assert the returned program equals the optimal one and its total cost is strictly less than the suboptimal alternative.

sub_tasks.requirements: The e-graph engine exposes the extension points required by Auto Vectorize and Auto Distribution.
Code has been implemented that allows external modules to register custom rewrite rules (e.g., MetaPackOperation, FoldNopPack, Boxing-insertion) into the shared saturation loop.

verification.spec: Register a dummy custom rewrite rule via the public registration API and run saturation on a small e-graph that triggers it. Assert the rule's callback is invoked and its resulting e-nodes are inserted. Also confirm that built-in rules (e.g., MetaPackOperation) are registered through the same mechanism.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that allows external modules to register per-operator cost functions and hard constraints (e.g., device memory capacity) that are added to the WPMAXSAT extraction problem.

verification.spec: Register a custom per-operator cost function and a hard constraint (e.g., 'total selected buffer size <= 1024') through the extraction API. Run extraction on an e-graph where the unconstrained optimum violates the constraint; assert the returned program satisfies the constraint and uses the custom cost weights.

sub_tasks.requirements: The engine ingests a computation graph (Relay/IR-level) and returns the extracted optimized computation graph in the same IR format, serving as the entry point invoked before Auto Schedule.

verification.spec: Feed a small computation graph in the compiler's IR to the e-graph optimization entry point and verify the returned artifact is in the same IR type, is semantically equivalent (matching outputs on random inputs), and is the object consumed by the subsequent Auto Schedule phase (verify via pipeline integration).

sub_tasks.requirements: The Auto Vectorize module implements MetaPackOperation and FoldNopPack e-graph rewrite rules to generate multiple packed layout candidates and eliminate redundant Pack/Unpack pairs, enabling optimal layout selection across heterogeneous compute units (scalar, vector, and tensor).
The MetaPackOperation rewrite rule is implemented and registered with the e-graph engine to non-destructively expand candidate packed layouts for each logical operator.

Code has been implemented for the MetaPackOperation rule that, given `Op(arg1, ..., argn)`, produces the rewritten form `Unpack(PackedOp(Pack(arg1, lanes1, axes1), ..., Pack(argn, lanesn, axesn)), axes^-1)` as specified in Table 2.

verification.spec: Construct an e-graph containing a single generic Op node with n>=2 arguments. Apply the MetaPackOperation rule. Assert that a new e-node is created with the structure Unpack(PackedOp(Pack(arg1, lanes1, axes1), ..., Pack(argn, lanesn, axesn)), axes_inv) and is unioned into the same e-class as the original Op. Verify by inspecting the e-class members.

sub_tasks.requirements: MetaPackOperation enumerates multiple hardware-specific packed variants per operator (e.g., 1D flat layout candidates for vector units and 2D blocked layout candidates for tensor/matrix units) rather than committing to a single layout.

verification.spec: Apply MetaPackOperation to a single operator (e.g., MatMul) in an e-graph seeded with a heterogeneous hardware descriptor exposing both a vector unit and a matrix unit. Assert the resulting e-class contains at least two distinct packed variants: one with 1D lanes (flat vector layout) and one with 2D blocked lanes (e.g., [16,16] tile axes).

sub_tasks.requirements: Packing factors (lanes) generated by MetaPackOperation are parameterized by the target hardware's vector/tensor unit widths so that the candidate lanes match the hardware SIMD/tensor tile dimensions (e.g., AVX2-width vectors, 16x16 blocks).

verification.spec: Run MetaPackOperation with two different hardware descriptors: one exposing AVX2 (8x fp32 lanes) and one exposing a 16x16 tensor tile. Assert the enumerated pack candidates include lanes of size 8 for the first and lanes of shape [16,16] for the second, i.e., candidate lanes are parameterized by hardware widths.

sub_tasks.requirements: MetaPackOperation is applied non-destructively via the e-graph: applying the rule adds new e-nodes into the appropriate e-class without removing or overwriting the original logical operator node.

verification.spec: Record the e-node set of the e-class containing the original operator before applying MetaPackOperation. Apply the rule and confirm the original e-node is still present in the same e-class (not removed) and that new packed-variant e-nodes have been added alongside it.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that for element-wise operators such as Exp, MetaPackOperation additionally emits a variant that operates directly on a blocked layout by treating the inner block (e.g., 16x16) as a contiguous vector, enabling pass-through across compute-memory-compute chains.

verification.spec: Apply MetaPackOperation to an elementwise Exp node inside an Attention-like subgraph MatMul(Exp(MatMul(Q,K)), V) whose adjacent MatMul e-nodes have a [16,16] blocked layout. Assert the Exp e-class includes a variant that consumes/produces the blocked layout directly (treating the 16x16 block as a length-256 contiguous vector), enabling FoldNopPack to eliminate intermediate Unpack/Pack.

sub_tasks.requirements: The rule engine terminates MetaPackOperation expansion (saturation or fuel/iteration limit) so that the e-graph reaches a stable state containing all considered pack candidates without infinite expansion.

verification.spec: Run e-graph saturation with MetaPackOperation enabled on a small graph and assert termination within a finite number of iterations (either a saturation fixed point where no new e-nodes are added, or a documented iteration/fuel cap). Verify the resulting e-graph is stable (running one more iteration produces no new e-nodes when saturation is reported).

sub_tasks.requirements: The FoldNopPack rewrite rule is implemented to eliminate redundant layout transformations by folding inverse Pack/Unpack pairs.
Code has been implemented for the FoldNopPack rule matching `Pack(Unpack(arg, ...), ...) -> arg` as specified in Table 2, registered in the same e-graph rewriting engine as MetaPackOperation.

verification.spec: Construct an e-graph containing a Pack(Unpack(x, params_u), params_p) expression. Apply the FoldNopPack rule via the same rewrite engine used by MetaPackOperation. Assert the resulting e-class contains an e-node equivalent to x (i.e., the outer Pack(Unpack(...)) is folded away and its e-class is unioned with x's e-class).

sub_tasks.requirements: FoldNopPack only fires when the Pack and Unpack it fuses have matching lanes and axes attributes so that they are true structural inverses; mismatched Pack/Unpack pairs are preserved.

verification.spec: Construct Pack(Unpack(x, axes=A1), lanes=L1, axes=A1) and confirm FoldNopPack rewrites it to x. Then construct Pack(Unpack(x, axes=A1), lanes=L2, axes=A2) with A2 != A1 or L2 != L1 and confirm FoldNopPack does NOT fire (the Pack/Unpack pair is preserved).

sub_tasks.requirements: On the Attention-like subgraph O = MatMul(Exp(MatMul(Q, K)), V), after saturating MetaPackOperation and FoldNopPack the e-graph must contain a candidate path in which the intermediate Unpack (after the first MatMul) and Pack (before the second MatMul) around Exp are eliminated, leaving data in the blocked hardware layout throughout the chain.

verification.spec: Build the graph O = MatMul(Exp(MatMul(Q, K)), V) in the compiler IR. Run equality saturation with only MetaPackOperation and FoldNopPack rules. Enumerate e-classes and assert there exists at least one program candidate in the saturated e-graph in which Exp is applied on packed (blocked) tensors directly, with NO Unpack node between the first MatMul and Exp AND no Pack node between Exp and the second MatMul.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Auto Vectorize module integrates with the Roofline-based cost model and the WPMAXSAT-based extractor so that from the set of packed candidates the extractor selects the layout plan minimizing data movement plus compute latency.

Cost weights are assigned to Pack, Unpack, and PackedOp e-nodes using the Roofline-based cost model (accounting for memory traffic of layout permutations and compute cycles of packed kernels), so that redundant Pack/Unpack sequences are penalized relative to pass-through blocked-layout variants.

verification.spec: Query the Roofline cost model for a Pack, an Unpack, and a PackedOp e-node given a hardware descriptor. Assert Pack/Unpack costs account for memory traffic (proportional to tensor bytes / bandwidth) and PackedOp cost accounts for compute cycles. Then build an e-graph with two extraction options, one with redundant Pack->Unpack->Pack and one blocked pass-through variant, and confirm the extractor picks the pass-through variant due to lower summed weights.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that hands the packed e-graph to the WPMAXSAT extractor and returns a single acyclic term-graph in which each e-class contributes exactly one selected e-node, giving one concrete layout plan per operator.

verification.spec: Pass a saturated e-graph containing multiple pack candidates to the WPMAXSAT extractor. Assert the returned artifact is a single acyclic term-graph, that each reachable e-class contributes exactly one e-node, and that each operator has one concrete (lanes, axes) layout plan (no e-class ambiguity remains).

sub_tasks.requirements: On the Attention-like example subgraph illustrated in Figure 3, running Auto Vectorize end-to-end (MetaPackOperation + FoldNopPack + cost-guided extraction) yields an extracted graph containing zero intermediate Unpack/Pack node pairs between the first MatMul, Exp, and the second MatMul.

verification.spec: Run the full Auto Vectorize pass (MetaPackOperation + FoldNopPack + cost-guided extraction with Roofline cost model) on the graph O = MatMul(Exp(MatMul(Q, K)), V). Traverse the extracted program and count Pack/Unpack node pairs on the path connecting first MatMul -> Exp -> second MatMul. Assert this count is 0.

sub_tasks.requirements: For a heterogeneous test subgraph containing an operator with a tensor-unit preferred (blocked) layout followed by a vector-unit operator, the extracted plan chooses different pack lanes/axes for the two operators when doing so lowers the modelled total cost compared to forcing a single uniform layout.

verification.spec: Construct a heterogeneous test subgraph: MatMul (tensor-unit blocked layout preferred) followed by a vector-unit-preferred operator (e.g., LayerNorm or Softmax). Compile with a hardware descriptor exposing both units and run extraction. Assert the extracted plan assigns different (lanes, axes) to the two operators AND that its modelled total cost is strictly less than the cost of a forced-uniform-layout plan (obtained by disabling MetaPackOperation).

sub_tasks.requirements: The Auto Vectorize module produces measurable end-to-end improvements attributable to layout optimization when combined with the rest of the nncase pipeline.

An ablation configuration is provided that disables MetaPackOperation and FoldNopPack (or forces a single default layout per operator) while keeping all other passes identical, so that the contribution of Auto Vectorize can be isolated by comparing token throughput on Qwen3-0.6B (F16, 1T) with and without the module.

verification.spec: Provide a compiler flag (e.g., --disable-auto-vectorize) that disables MetaPackOperation and FoldNopPack (or forces a single default layout). Build Qwen3-0.6B (F16) with and without the flag, run 1T single-core decode throughput on AMD Ryzen 9 5900X (or equivalent), and assert the baseline (auto-vectorize enabled) achieves ~13.87 tokens/s while the ablated variant is measurably lower.

sub_tasks.requirements: For the Attention-like subgraph in Figure 3, a count of the number of Pack plus Unpack nodes in the final generated code path is reported; with Auto Vectorize enabled the number of intermediate Pack/Unpack pairs between the MatMul-Exp-MatMul chain is zero, whereas with FoldNopPack disabled the count is strictly greater than zero.

verification.spec: Build the Attention-like subgraph O = MatMul(Exp(MatMul(Q,K)), V) as an nncase IR. Compile once with Auto Vectorize + FoldNopPack enabled and once with FoldNopPack disabled. Traverse the resulting IR/graph and count Pack and Unpack nodes on the data path between the two MatMuls. Assert that the enabled configuration yields zero intermediate Pack/Unpack pairs on that chain, and that the disabled configuration yields strictly more (>=2).

sub_tasks.requirements: The SBP-abstraction-based distributed strategy search on the e-graph with joint cost modeling and memory constraints is implemented (Section 3.1.3, Figures 4-6).
SBP abstraction primitives and N-Dimensional SBP representation are implemented.

Code has been implemented that defines the three SBP primitives: Split(S) with a specified tensor axis, Broadcast(B), and Partial(P) with a specified reduction operation, each usable as a per-dimension distribution descriptor.

verification.spec: Import the SBP module and verify three primitive classes/factories exist: Split(axis=int), Broadcast(), and Partial(reduce_op). Instantiate Split(0), Split(1), Broadcast(), Partial('sum'); assert each has an identifying type tag ('S'/'B'/'P') and that Split carries an axis attribute and Partial carries a reduction op attribute.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for an ND-SBP vector type P_nd = [sbp_0, sbp_1, ..., sbp_{N-1}] that composes SBP primitives across N orthogonal placement dimensions.

verification.spec: Import the ND-SBP type and construct P_nd = [S(0), B, P] over an N=3 placement. Assert the object stores an ordered sequence of length N whose elements are SBP primitives (Split/Broadcast/Partial), and that indexing/iteration returns them in order. Verify that constructing with a length mismatched to the placement rank raises.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for a Placement type that maps physical devices onto a multi-dimensional logical array whose axes correspond to the dimensions of the ND-SBP vector.

verification.spec: Instantiate Placement with a nested device list like [[0,1],[2,3]] and verify: (a) it exposes a multi-dimensional shape (e.g., (2,2)); (b) each axis of the shape aligns with a dimension of an ND-SBP; (c) constructing an ND-SBP whose rank does not match Placement rank is rejected.

sub_tasks.requirements: The SBP + Placement combination correctly materializes distributed tensor tiles: given a [2,2] tensor and a 1D placement over 2 devices with S(0), each device receives the expected row shard as illustrated in Figure 4(a).

verification.spec: Create a [2,2] tensor with known values, a 1D Placement over 2 devices, and apply SBP=[S(0)]. Materialize the per-device shards and assert device 0 receives row 0 and device 1 receives row 1, matching Figure 4(a). Repeat with S(1) and assert column-wise sharding.

sub_tasks.requirements: The ND-SBP mechanism handles nested placements: for a 2-level topology (e.g., 2 groups of 2 devices as in Figure 4(b)), a 2D SBP such as [S(0), S(1)] produces the correct nested tensor distribution.

verification.spec: Create a [4,4] tensor, 2D Placement of shape (2,2) representing 2 groups of 2 devices, apply ND-SBP=[S(0), S(1)]. Assert the resulting 4 per-device shards each have shape [2,2] and content matches the block partition [i*2:(i+1)*2, j*2:(j+1)*2] as shown in Figure 4(b).

sub_tasks.requirements: SBP Signatures and the Boxing communication primitive are implemented.
Code has been implemented that defines an SBP Signature per operator enumerating the set of valid input-output SBP combinations for that operator's semantics.

verification.spec: For a set of representative operators (element-wise Add, MatMul, Reduce), query the compiler's SBP Signature registry and assert it returns a non-empty enumeration of (input_SBPs -> output_SBP) tuples. Verify each entry is semantically legal per SBP rules (e.g., MatMul supports S(0)xB -> S(0), BxS(1) -> S(1), etc.).

sub_tasks.requirements: For element-wise binary operators (e.g., addition C = A + B), the signature enumeration accepts consistent SBP combinations (e.g., both operands S(0)) and rejects incompatible ones (e.g., S(0) vs. S(1)) as illegal without redistribution.

verification.spec: Query the SBP Signature for element-wise binary Add. Assert (S(0),S(0))->S(0) and (B,B)->B are accepted, and (S(0),S(1)) is rejected/not present (matching Eq. 2 in the paper).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for a unified Box(v, sbp) communication primitive that wraps a tensor with a distributed SBP state so that any distributed op is formalized as Box(Op(Box(A, P))).

verification.spec: Construct a simple logical op (e.g., MatMul) on a tensor A. Wrap as Box(Op(Box(A, sbp_in)), sbp_out). Verify Box accepts a tensor and an SBP state, produces a node with .tensor and .sbp fields, and that a distributed lowering pass emits communication primitives (split/allgather/allreduce/identity) consistent with the input->output SBP transition for at least three cases: S(0)->B, P->B (allreduce), S(0)->S(1) (resharding).

sub_tasks.requirements: The Boxing primitive dispatches to concrete collective operations covering splitting, broadcasting, aggregation (all-reduce over Partial), and resharding (SBP-to-SBP) as required to satisfy the target SBP.

verification.spec: Instantiate a Box operator with each of the following (src_sbp -> dst_sbp) transitions: B->S (split/scatter), S->B (all-gather), P->B (all-reduce), S(0)->S(1) (resharding). Trace/inspect the dispatched collective and assert each maps to the expected collective op name. Additionally run on a mock/local multi-device backend and assert output values are correct.

sub_tasks.requirements: The distributed e-graph search space is constructed directly from the logical computation graph using the E-Cluster abstraction and the three-phase algorithm of Figure 5.

Code has been implemented for an E-Cluster data structure that maps each logical node to a dictionary keyed by SBP signature whose values are e-class IDs, so that nodes with identical computation logic and SBP attributes are unified.

verification.spec: Import the E-Cluster class. Create one for a logical node, insert distributed e-nodes with two distinct SBP signatures, and verify: (a) it behaves as a dict keyed by SBP signature; (b) values are e-class IDs; (c) inserting a second e-node with an already-present SBP unions into the existing e-class rather than creating a new key.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for the Input Phase (Fig. 5 lines 5-11): for each graph input v it enumerates feasible SBP candidates via GetSBPs(v), instantiates Box(v, s) nodes, groups them by SBP, and registers the resulting e-classes into memo[v].

verification.spec: Construct a minimal logical graph with a single input tensor v. Run BuildEGraph and inspect memo[v]: assert it contains one e-class per SBP returned by GetSBPs(v), each e-class containing a Box(v, s) node. Verify that for a placement of size k, the number of distinct SBP keys equals |GetSBPs(v)|.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for the Compute Phase that topologically sorts non-input nodes and, for each node, gathers candidate input e-classes from memo including newly generated Resharding Boxing candidates (GenReshard) to prevent search-space shrinkage.

verification.spec: Build a two-op chain (Input -> Op1 -> Op2). Run BuildEGraph and verify topological visit order. For Op2, inspect the collected input candidates and assert they include: (a) all e-classes already present in memo[Op1] (reuse), and (b) additional Resharding Boxing candidates generated by GenReshard, i.e., the candidate set is strictly larger than memo[Op1].values().

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that takes the Cartesian product of candidate input e-classes, filters each combination against the operator's SBP Signature via IsValid(v, args), and instantiates a distributed compute e-node only for legal combinations.

verification.spec: For an element-wise Add node with two input candidate sets each containing {S(0), S(1), B}, run the Compute-phase expansion and count instantiated compute e-nodes. Assert only combinations matching the Add SBP Signature (e.g., (S(0),S(0)), (S(1),S(1)), (B,B), plus valid Partial cases) are created; combinations like (S(0),S(1)) are excluded.

sub_tasks.requirements: Distributed compute nodes that produce the same output SBP are merged into a single e-class via the e-graph Union operation (Fig. 5 line 36), keeping the search graph compact.

verification.spec: Construct a case where two distinct legal input SBP combinations for an operator (e.g., MatMul with (S(0),B) and (B via resharded S(0),B)) yield the same output SBP. After BuildEGraph, assert that both compute e-nodes end up in a single e-class in memo[op] (i.e., the number of keys in memo[op] equals the number of distinct output SBPs, not the number of input combinations).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for the Output Phase (Fig. 5 lines 39-43) that appends Unshard Boxing nodes on each output e-class to Host placement and unions them so downstream extraction can retrieve a globally consistent result.

verification.spec: Build an e-graph for a graph with a single output. Inspect the graph after the Output phase and assert: (a) for each e-class in memo[output], a Box(_, Host) node has been added; (b) all these Host-target boxes are unioned into a single e-class so extraction sees a unique output root.

sub_tasks.requirements: On a small representative subgraph (e.g., a MatMul with two inputs as in Figure 6), the constructed distributed e-graph contains a MatMul e-cluster with multiple e-classes corresponding to distinct valid SBP signatures, all connected through Boxing nodes.

verification.spec: Build a MatMul(A,B) subgraph on a 2-device placement. Run distributed e-graph construction and assert that memo[MatMul] contains >= 3 distinct SBP-keyed e-classes (e.g., outputs S(0), S(1), P), each backed by at least one compute e-node whose inputs are reached via Boxing nodes from A/B's e-cluster (matching Figure 6).

sub_tasks.requirements: Communication cost model based on Roofline and Alpha-Beta (latency-bandwidth) MPI modeling is implemented for edge weights in the distributed e-graph.

Code has been implemented that computes the simulated communication time for each Boxing/Resharding pattern using an Alpha-Beta (latency alpha + message_size / bandwidth beta) model parameterized per collective type.

verification.spec: Call the communication cost function for several Boxing patterns (all-gather 1MB on 2 devices, resharding S(0)->S(1) on 4 devices, broadcast 8MB). Assert returned cost obeys the form alpha + size/beta with the configured per-collective (alpha,beta) constants. Varying message size linearly while holding alpha,beta fixed must produce a linear cost curve with slope 1/beta and intercept alpha (verified by linear fit residual < 1e-6).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes per-operator computation cost using the Roofline model (min of compute-bound and bandwidth-bound throughput) and combines it with communication cost into a joint edge cost on distributed e-nodes.

verification.spec: For a MatMul with configurable FLOPs and bytes and hardware (peak_flops, peak_bw), evaluate the compute cost function and assert it equals max(FLOPs/peak_flops, bytes/peak_bw) (Roofline). Then evaluate the joint edge cost on a distributed e-node whose Boxing has known comm cost c_comm and assert total_cost = f(compute_cost, c_comm) with both terms materially contributing (e.g., total strictly increases if either component increases).

sub_tasks.requirements: Cost tables for standard collective patterns (all-reduce, all-gather, reduce-scatter, broadcast, split, resharding) are implemented following the MPICH-style formulas referenced by Thakur et al., not just a single flat estimate.

verification.spec: Enumerate the cost-model registry and assert distinct callables/entries exist for at least: all-reduce, all-gather, reduce-scatter, broadcast, split/scatter, and resharding. For each, verify the cost formula depends on P (number of devices) non-trivially, matching the log(P) / (P-1)/P style Thakur MPICH formulas (e.g., all-reduce cost != broadcast cost for P>=4 on the same message).

sub_tasks.requirements: For a canonical test case (e.g., a MatMul with S(0)xB vs. BxS(1) input strategies), the cost model returns strictly different total costs, and the ordering matches the theoretical Alpha-Beta prediction.

verification.spec: Construct a MatMul(A[M,K], B[K,N]) with M=N=K=1024 on 4 devices. Query total cost for input strategy1=(S(0),B) and strategy2=(B,S(1)). Assert the two costs differ (|c1-c2|/max(c1,c2) > 1e-3) and that their ordering matches the Alpha-Beta analytic prediction computed directly from the formulas (i.e., cheaper strategy per hand calculation is also the one returned as cheaper by the model).

sub_tasks.requirements: Memory capacity is enforced as a hard constraint during distributed strategy extraction.
Code has been implemented that computes, for each candidate distributed e-node, the per-device memory footprint (activations + weights) implied by its SBP attributes and placement.

verification.spec: For a MatMul with weight W[1024,1024] fp16 (2MB) on 2 devices, compute per-device memory for SBP=B (should be ~2MB per device for W) and SBP=S(0) (should be ~1MB per device). Assert values match analytic expectation within 5%. Repeat for activations to confirm activation-size accounting is included, not only weights.

sub_tasks.requirements: Extraction rejects any strategy for which the summed per-device memory requirements exceed the configured cluster memory capacity, treating capacity as a hard SAT constraint rather than a soft penalty.

verification.spec: Set an artificially tight per-device memory capacity (e.g., 512KB) and run extraction on a graph where the only broadcast-heavy (low-comm) strategy exceeds capacity but a higher-communication sharded strategy fits. Assert (a) the solver returns UNSAT or a strategy without any capacity-violating selection, and (b) the returned strategy is the sharded one, not the broadcast one, even though its cost is higher.

sub_tasks.requirements: When a naive Broadcast-heavy strategy would OOM under a user-provided device capacity, the extractor deterministically returns a memory-feasible alternative (e.g., a Split-based strategy) instead of failing silently.

verification.spec: Build a small distributed e-graph for a MatMul with two devices. Set per-device memory capacity such that a fully Broadcast strategy for the weight tensor exceeds capacity while a Split(0) strategy fits. Run the SAT-based extractor and assert (1) it returns a valid strategy, (2) the extracted strategy for the weight is Split (not Broadcast), and (3) per-device memory sum <= capacity.

sub_tasks.requirements: Optimal distributed strategy extraction from the distributed e-graph is implemented as a constrained WPMAXSAT problem solved with an off-the-shelf solver.

Code has been implemented that encodes distributed e-node selection as boolean variables and adds acyclicity/one-e-node-per-e-class constraints so that exactly one distributed variant is selected per logical node.

verification.spec: Invoke the encoder on a small distributed e-graph and dump the generated SAT/CP-SAT model. Assert: (a) one boolean var per candidate distributed e-node; (b) for each e-class, a constraint sum(selected)==1 (exactly-one); (c) acyclicity/consistency constraints so that if a compute e-node is selected, exactly one variant of each of its input e-classes is also selected.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that adds the memory-capacity hard constraints and encodes the joint compute+communication cost as WPMAXSAT weights on selection variables.

verification.spec: Inspect the encoded model and assert: (a) presence of per-storage-level linear constraints of the form sum(mem_i * x_i) <= C_l (hard); (b) the objective is a weighted sum of selection variables with weights equal to the joint compute+communication costs from the cost model (WPMAXSAT-style). Flip a weight by hand and re-solve; verify the optimal selection changes accordingly.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that invokes a solver (e.g., OR-Tools CP-SAT / MaxSAT backend) and reconstructs the chosen distributed subgraph (selected SBPs plus Boxing operations) from the solver's assignment.

verification.spec: Run the extractor end-to-end on a small chain (Input -> MatMul -> Add -> Output) using OR-Tools CP-SAT (or configured MaxSAT backend). Assert: (a) the solver returns status OPTIMAL/FEASIBLE; (b) the reconstructed subgraph contains exactly one selected variant per logical node with concrete SBPs; (c) Boxing operators appear on edges where source and destination SBPs differ.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Auto Distribution module integrates end-to-end with the rest of the compiler and supports the unified single-node/multi-node NUMA abstraction claimed by the paper.

Code has been implemented that connects the Auto Distribution pass to the shared e-graph produced by earlier passes so distribution search coexists with (rather than replaces) Auto Vectorize rewrites.

verification.spec: Inspect the compiler pipeline entry point for Auto Distribution: verify it accepts an e-graph handle produced by prior passes (Auto Vectorize) rather than constructing a fresh IR. Check that after Auto Distribution runs, the e-graph still contains e-nodes/e-classes introduced by Auto Vectorize (e.g., PackedOp e-nodes are still present alongside distributed Boxing e-nodes). Confirm via unit test that a minimal graph passed through Auto Vectorize then Auto Distribution retains vectorization e-classes.

sub_tasks.requirements: Auto Distribution treats individual CPU cores of a single machine as logical distributed nodes (per the 'unified distributed compilation' paradigm) so the same pipeline is used for 1T, 4T, and 8T configurations without switching backends.

verification.spec: Compile the same Qwen3 model with thread counts 1, 4, and 8 using the same compilation entry point / config schema. Verify no branch switches to a different backend/pipeline; the Placement/topology description should be the only thing that changes (e.g., [1], [4], [8]). Assert that internal pass logs show Auto Distribution runs in all three cases.

sub_tasks.requirements: Distributed strategies selected by Auto Distribution are lowered into the NTTD (distributed NTT) template configurations (mesh topology + shard_policy) so downstream codegen produces statically-bound collective calls.

verification.spec: Compile a small distributed subgraph and inspect the generated C++ code: verify that NTTD template instantiations appear (e.g., shard_policy::S<...>, mesh topology template arguments) and that these template parameters correspond to the SBP strategy selected by Auto Distribution. Grep generated sources for 'shard_policy' / 'NTTD' / 'mesh' template usage; confirm no runtime-dispatched policy strings.

sub_tasks.requirements: Constants/weights are pre-split and pinned according to the SBP attributes chosen by Auto Distribution, so no runtime resharding of weights is emitted for a fixed deployment.

verification.spec: Compile a two-core distributed configuration for a linear model with a weight tensor. Inspect the emitted constant blobs / weight files: verify that constants are pre-split per SBP attribute (e.g., two shards for S(0) on 2 devices), and that the generated runtime code contains no resharding/scatter of weights during inference. Assert per-core weight bytes ≈ total_weight_bytes / num_cores for Split axes and equal to total for Broadcast axes.

sub_tasks.requirements: The compile-time static task partitioning path is exercised end-to-end (no runtime OpenMP fork-join scheduling on the critical path) for the multi-core Qwen3 execution flow.

verification.spec: Grep the generated multi-core Qwen3 runtime C++ sources for '#pragma omp', 'omp_parallel', 'omp_get_thread_num', or dynamic task scheduling APIs. Verify these do not appear on the decoding hot path. Instead, verify presence of statically-partitioned per-core kernel launches (e.g., static thread barriers or precomputed per-core work assignments).

sub_tasks.requirements: Measured behavioral properties attributable to Auto Distribution on Qwen3 workloads are reproduced.
For Qwen3-1.7B-F16, going from 1T to 4T with Auto Distribution enabled yields a throughput gain of approximately 74% (vs. only ~32% for llama.cpp), as reported in Section 4.2.

verification.spec: Run Qwen3-1.7B-F16 through the nncase pipeline at 1T and 4T on the reference AMD Ryzen 9 5900X platform (or nearest available x86 CPU). Measure decode throughput (tokens/s) with batch=1, 8-token prompt, 100 repeats. Compute gain = (throughput_4T - throughput_1T) / throughput_1T. Expect ≈0.74.

sub_tasks.requirements: With Auto Distribution enabled, no OOM occurs when running Qwen3-1.7B-F16 on the 4T/8T configuration of the AMD Ryzen 9 5900X + 128GB DDR4 setup, i.e., the memory-capacity SAT constraint keeps per-core footprint within the machine's memory.

verification.spec: Compile and run Qwen3-1.7B-F16 with nncase Auto Distribution at 4T and 8T on a 128GB DDR4 machine. Monitor peak resident memory via /usr/bin/time -v or psutil. Assert the process completes decoding of at least 32 tokens without OOM and peak RSS < 128GB. Confirm the SAT-solved plan reports per-core memory within the configured capacity.

sub_tasks.requirements: Disabling the Resharding Boxing generation (GenReshard) in the Compute Phase measurably degrades the extracted plan's cost on a canonical MatMul chain, confirming that resharding candidates are necessary to avoid a shrinking search space.

verification.spec: On a canonical MatMul chain (e.g., 3 stacked MatMuls with shape [4,4]) run Auto Distribution twice: (a) with GenReshard enabled (default), (b) with GenReshard disabled (returns empty resharding candidates). Compare the extracted plan's cost model score. Assert cost(b) > cost(a), i.e. disabling resharding produces a strictly worse (or equal-but-not-better) plan, confirming resharding is beneficial.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Tiered Tile Graph representation and MCTS-based structural search (merge/reorder actions) are implemented.
The Tiered Tile Graph data structure representing hierarchical nested tiles across memory levels is implemented.

Code has been implemented that defines a node type representing a tile at memory level n, containing a loop set {l_i^n} and a topologically-ordered list of child sub-graph nodes at level n-1, consistent with the recursive definition Op_a^n = ({l_i^n}, (Op_a^{n-1}, ...)) from Section 3.2.2.

verification.spec: Import the tile node class (e.g., TiledTileNode or TileGraphNode) and verify via reflection/inspection that instances at level n expose a loop set field (list of loop objects representing {l_i^n}) and a children field that is an ordered list of tile nodes at level n-1. Construct a two-level example and assert child.level == parent.level - 1 and that children order matches topological order of the source subgraph.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that Tiered Tile Graph nodes carry polyhedral / affine map information describing the iteration-domain mapping between a child tile's loops and the loops of its parent tile (as illustrated by the R_{Op2^2 Op1^1} affine map in Figure 7).

verification.spec: Build a Tiered Tile Graph with a parent tile and a child tile and inspect the child node's attached polyhedral/affine map field. Verify it encodes a mapping from the parent's (d_i, t_i) domain to the child's loop domain (e.g., an isl-style affine map object or an equivalent tuple-of-expressions structure). Round-trip a known map like ((d0,t0),(d1,t1),(d2,t2)) -> ((d0,t0),(d1,t1)) and assert equality.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that constructs an initial Tiered Tile Graph from an input single-core subgraph, mapping each operator into its own tile hierarchy with outer loops as root nodes and inner loops as child nodes as described in Section 3.2.

verification.spec: Call the initial-Tiered-Tile-Graph builder on a small 2-operator single-core subgraph (e.g., MatMul -> Add). Assert the result contains one tile per operator, outer loops of each operator are attached to the root-level tile node, and inner loops to nested child tiles, matching the description in Section 3.2.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that supports multiple memory levels (at minimum L0 register, L1, L2, and top-level main memory) as distinct levels within the Tiered Tile Graph, so that fusion and buffer placement decisions can reference these levels by name/index.

verification.spec: Query the memory-hierarchy configuration API. Assert at least 4 named/indexed levels are supported (L0 register, L1, L2, top-level DRAM). Build a tile whose buffer placement references each of these levels and verify no error. Confirm that fusion actions can accept any of these level indices as a parameter.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Tiered Tile Graph exposes a serialization or printing routine that renders a graph state in the tile-centric notation used in Figure 7 (nested (loops, child tiles) form), enabling deterministic identification of distinct structural states.

verification.spec: Call a to_string / serialize method on a Tiered Tile Graph containing two nested tiles. Assert the output is a nested-form string of shape roughly ({loops}, (child_tile, ...)) matching the tile-centric notation of Figure 7. Build two structurally identical graphs and confirm serialization yields identical strings (deterministic canonical form); build a structurally different graph and confirm serialization differs.

sub_tasks.requirements: The structural transformation actions (merge and reorder) that traverse the Tiered Tile Graph state space are implemented.

Code has been implemented for a merge(src, dst, level) action that migrates all subgraphs of a source tile node into a destination tile node at the specified memory level, fusing their loop scopes as described in Section 3.2.1.

verification.spec: Construct a Tiered Tile Graph with a source tile containing sub-tiles and a separate destination tile at a target memory level. Invoke merge(src, dst, level). Assert: (1) source's subgraphs are now children of dst at the specified level; (2) src is removed from its previous position; (3) loop scopes of src and dst are fused at the target level.

sub_tasks.requirements: Applying merge(1, 2, 2) to the illustrative two-operator graph from Section 3.2.1 produces a state in which Op1^1 becomes a child of Op2^2 at Level 2 (i.e. Op1 and Op2 are fused at L2), matching the state transition shown in the paper.

verification.spec: Recreate the Section 3.2.1 illustrative two-operator graph (Op1, Op2 as in Figure 7). Invoke merge(1, 2, 2). Serialize the resulting Tiered Tile Graph and assert Op1^1 appears as a child of Op2^2 at Level 2, matching the state transition depicted in the paper.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for a reorder(i, n, loops) action that reconfigures the execution order of the loop set of a specific tile Op_i^n according to a supplied permutation, without altering other tiles.

verification.spec: Construct a tile Op_i^n with loop set [l0, l1, l2]. Invoke reorder(i, n, [2, 0, 1]). Assert the loop set of that specific tile is now [l2, l0, l1] and all other tiles' loop orderings are unchanged.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that enumerates the set of legal merge and reorder actions available from a given Tiered Tile Graph state, rejecting actions that would violate dependency ordering or memory-level nesting invariants.

verification.spec: Given a Tiered Tile Graph, call the legal-actions enumerator. Verify: (1) the returned list contains only merge/reorder tuples; (2) attempting merge(src, dst, level) where src depends transitively on dst (would violate dependency order) is not present; (3) attempting to merge into a level deeper than the destination tile's own level is not present.

sub_tasks.requirements: The merge and reorder actions preserve the original computation-graph dependencies: applying any legal sequence of actions yields a Tiered Tile Graph whose contracted dataflow is semantically equivalent to the input subgraph (verifiable via a topological-consistency check on child tile order).

verification.spec: Take a small computation subgraph (Op1 -> Op2 -> Op3), build its initial Tiered Tile Graph, and apply a random sequence of 5 legal merge/reorder actions. For the resulting graph, extract the contracted dataflow (topological order of leaf tiles) and assert it is a valid topological order of the original DAG (Op1 before Op2 before Op3). Repeat 20 times.

sub_tasks.requirements: The MCTS search driver over structural states with the four MCTS phases is implemented.

Code has been implemented that builds an MCTS search tree whose root is initialized from the raw computation subgraph's Tiered Tile Graph, whose nodes represent Tiered Tile Graph states, and whose edges are labeled with merge/reorder actions.

verification.spec: Instantiate the MCTS driver on a small subgraph. Inspect the built tree: the root node's state equals the initial Tiered Tile Graph of the raw subgraph; each non-root node's state is a Tiered Tile Graph; each edge stores an action of the form ('merge', src, dst, level) or ('reorder', i, n, perm).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for the MCTS Selection phase, descending from the root by choosing children according to a UCB-style exploration/exploitation tradeoff over previously observed rewards.

verification.spec: Manually seed an MCTS tree with two child nodes having known (visit_count, total_reward). Invoke the Selection routine and assert it returns the child maximizing a UCB-style formula (Q + c*sqrt(ln(N_parent)/n_child)). Test with several combinations where high-value-low-visit and low-value-high-visit alternate, confirming the exploration term matters.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for the MCTS Expansion phase, which generates child states of a selected tree node by applying legal merge/reorder actions enumerated from the current Tiered Tile Graph.

verification.spec: Invoke the Expansion routine on a leaf MCTS node whose state is a known Tiered Tile Graph. Assert the number of newly created children equals the number of legal actions enumerated from that state, and each child's state equals the parent's state with the corresponding merge/reorder applied.

sub_tasks.requirements: The MCTS Simulation phase is implemented as a deterministic analytical evaluation (not a random rollout): it invokes the MINLP parametric-optimization solver on the leaf structural state and uses the solver's estimated latency as the simulation reward, as specified in Section 3.2.1.

verification.spec: Invoke the Simulation routine on an MCTS leaf twice with the same input state. Assert both calls return identical reward (determinism). Instrument the MINLP solver entry point and assert it is called during Simulation (i.e., no random rollout code path is taken). Assert the returned reward is a function of the MINLP-reported estimated latency (e.g., reward = -latency or 1/latency).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for the MCTS Backpropagation phase, propagating simulation rewards from evaluated leaves up to the root while updating per-node visit counts and value estimates.

verification.spec: Build an MCTS tree with a known path root->A->B->leaf. Manually set leaf simulation reward to r. Invoke Backpropagation. Assert visit_count of A, B, leaf, and root each increment by 1, and total_reward of each ancestor increases by r (or by r/N under an averaging scheme, consistently).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that runs the MCTS loop until a configurable termination condition (iteration budget or convergence criterion) is met and then returns the best-observed Tiered Tile Graph structural state together with its parametric solution as the output of Auto Schedule structural search.

verification.spec: Run the MCTS driver on a small subgraph with iteration budget = 50. Assert the driver terminates within budget and returns a tuple (best_structural_state: TieredTileGraph, best_parametric_solution). Confirm the returned reward equals the maximum reward observed across all evaluated leaves. Also test a convergence-based termination path if configured.

sub_tasks.requirements: The MCTS driver caches the analytical simulation result for each distinct structural state (keyed by the canonical Tiered Tile Graph serialization), so revisiting an already-evaluated state does not re-invoke the MINLP solver.

verification.spec: Instrument the MINLP solver entry with a call counter. Run MCTS such that some tree paths lead to the same canonical Tiered Tile Graph state. Assert the MINLP call counter is strictly less than the number of Simulation invocations, i.e., cached results were reused. Verify that the cache key equals the canonical serialization of the state (setting the same state twice yields one MINLP call).

sub_tasks.requirements: Integration of structural MCTS search into the end-to-end Auto Schedule pipeline is exercised and validated.

Code has been implemented that, for each single-core subgraph produced by the front-end passes, converts it into a Tiered Tile Graph and invokes the MCTS structural search followed by parametric optimization, matching the pipeline described in Section 3.

verification.spec: Import the Auto Schedule pipeline entry point and confirm that, given a single-core subgraph IR, it (a) constructs a Tiered Tile Graph object, (b) invokes an MCTS structural search routine, and (c) invokes a parametric optimization (MINLP) routine, in that order. Verify via code inspection (grep/AST) and by tracing calls on a small toy subgraph.

sub_tasks.requirements: For an Attention-like fusion subgraph (e.g. MatMul-Exp-MatMul as used elsewhere in the paper), the MCTS structural search discovers a fused structural state where at least one intermediate producer is nested as a child tile of its consumer at an on-chip memory level (L1 or L2), demonstrating operator fusion via the merge action.

verification.spec: Construct a MatMul-Exp-MatMul subgraph and run the MCTS structural search. Inspect the returned Tiered Tile Graph and assert that at least one producer tile is nested as a child of its consumer tile at memory level L1 or L2 (i.e., a merge(src,dst,level<=2) action was applied). Fail if the returned structure is the trivial unfused root-level layout.

sub_tasks.requirements: The structural state returned by MCTS for a given subgraph has a MINLP-evaluated latency no worse than the latency of the initial (unfused, default-ordered) Tiered Tile Graph state for the same subgraph, confirming that MCTS improves upon the baseline structure.

verification.spec: For a fixed test subgraph (e.g., MatMul-Exp-MatMul), evaluate the MINLP-estimated latency of the initial unfused Tiered Tile Graph state and of the state returned by MCTS. Assert latency(MCTS_result) <= latency(initial_state).

sub_tasks.requirements: The MINLP-based tile size and buffer placement solver with static analysis and constraints is implemented (Section 3.2.2).
The MINLP variable definitions for tile sizes and buffer placement are implemented.
Code has been implemented that defines TileVar(l, op, i) as an integer variable per (memory level, operator, loop index), representing the tile size at that loop.

verification.spec: Inspect the MINLP variable-construction code and verify that a TileVar variable is instantiated per (memory level l, operator op, loop index i) triple, declared as an integer variable in the solver (e.g., OR-Tools IntVar). Confirm by constructing variables for a toy 2-op subgraph and checking the resulting variable dict keys match (l,op,i).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that defines Place(cl, b, e, sl) as a boolean variable characterizing whether buffer b created at level cl at entry position e is stored at level sl.

verification.spec: Inspect the MINLP variable-construction code and verify that a boolean/0-1 variable Place(cl, b, e, sl) is created for each valid (creation level, buffer, entry, storage level) tuple. On a toy buffer with 2 memory levels, confirm the variables exist and are booleans.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Place variable domain restricts storage level sl to be at or below the creation level cl (sl <= cl), rejecting placements into faster levels than the buffer was created at.

verification.spec: Enumerate the Place variables generated for a toy buffer with multiple memory levels and assert no variable is created with sl > cl (storage level shallower/faster than creation level). Equivalently, attempt to add a Place(cl=1, b, e, sl=0) constraint set to 1 and verify the solver reports infeasibility or the variable is absent.

sub_tasks.requirements: TileVar variables are bounded to be strictly positive integers so they can serve as loop tile factors in the MINLP formulation.

verification.spec: Inspect the domain declared for TileVar variables in the MINLP builder and assert the lower bound is >= 1 (strictly positive integer). Instantiate variables for a toy subgraph and confirm solver bounds.

sub_tasks.requirements: Static analysis expressions over the Tiered Tile Graph are implemented to derive extents, buffer sizes, trip counts, and data traffic as functions of the MINLP variables.
Code has been implemented that computes the backward Extent recursively across memory levels, using the relation R to determine when adjacent-level loops map to the same iteration variable.

verification.spec: Construct a 2-level Tiered Tile Graph with a known relation R that maps adjacent-level loops to the same iteration variable in some cases and different in others. Call the Extent computation and verify the returned symbolic expression recursively references parent-level extents when R indicates loop coalescing, and equals TileVar otherwise.

sub_tasks.requirements: Extent computation correctly returns TileVar * ParentExtent when adjacent-level loops map to the same iteration variable, and TileVar alone otherwise, matching Section 3.2.2's recursive Extent formula.

verification.spec: For a toy tile graph, evaluate Extent under two scenarios: (i) adjacent levels share an iteration variable — expect Extent = TileVar * ParentExtent; (ii) adjacent levels are independent — expect Extent = TileVar. Assert the returned symbolic expressions match these forms by substituting concrete TileVar values.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes BufferSize(b) by applying the buffer's access relation A_op^b to the extents of the enclosing loops.

verification.spec: Construct a buffer b with a known affine access relation A (e.g., 2D read [i,j]) and enclosing loop extents. Call the BufferSize(b) routine and verify the returned symbolic expression equals the product of the mapped extents per access-relation dimension.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes the TripCount at a given level as the product of TileVars from the current level down to the innermost level.

verification.spec: Build a 3-level tile graph with TileVars [t2, t1, t0]. Compute TripCount at each level and verify: TripCount(level=2) == t2*t1*t0, TripCount(level=1) == t1*t0, TripCount(level=0) == t0 (product from current level down to innermost).

sub_tasks.requirements: Buffers are partitioned into read-only (B_read) and read-write (B_write) sets so that data-traffic expressions can distinguish read from write accesses when computing traffic per level.

verification.spec: Inspect the traffic-computation module and verify that buffers are classified into two disjoint sets B_read and B_write (or an equivalent flag distinguishing read vs read-write). Confirm on a toy graph that an input operand appears in B_read and an output operand in B_write.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes total data traffic at memory level l by summing, over all buffers, TripCount * BufferSize contributions, gated by the Place variables indicating storage at that level.

verification.spec: For a toy 2-buffer subgraph with known TripCount and BufferSize, evaluate the data-traffic expression at level l. Verify the expression sums over buffers of TripCount(l)*BufferSize(b), each term gated by the Place(_,b,_,sl=l) boolean variable. Substituting Place=1 for one buffer and 0 for the other should yield only that buffer's contribution.

sub_tasks.requirements: The MINLP constraint set enforcing legality of tilings and buffer placements is implemented.
Domain-bounds constraint has been implemented that requires the extent at the top memory level (L_top) to cover the original iteration domain shape of each loop.

verification.spec: Build a MINLP model with a known iteration-domain shape S per loop. Assert the model contains a constraint Extent_at_top_level(loop) >= S for each loop. Verify infeasibility if TileVars are forced smaller than needed to cover S.

sub_tasks.requirements: I/O buffer placement constraint has been implemented that forces graph-input and graph-output buffers to reside in the outermost memory level.

verification.spec: Build a toy subgraph with a graph-input tensor and graph-output tensor. Inspect the MINLP constraints and verify that for these buffers, Place(_,b,_,sl=outermost)==1 is enforced. Attempting to set their storage level to an inner level should render the model infeasible.

sub_tasks.requirements: Innermost-cache constraint has been implemented that requires the active computation buffer at level 0 to be stored there for the operator to execute.

verification.spec: For a toy op with an active compute buffer b_active, verify the MINLP model contains a constraint that at least one Place(_, b_active, _, sl=0) variable equals 1 during execution of that op. Removing this constraint should allow infeasible-for-execution placements.

sub_tasks.requirements: Unique-storage constraint has been implemented that requires each buffer to be stored exactly once across the set of valid storage levels.

verification.spec: For each buffer b in a toy model, verify a constraint sum_{sl in valid_levels} Place(cl,b,e,sl) == 1 exists (unique storage). Attempting to satisfy the model with two Place variables set to 1 for the same buffer/entry should be infeasible.

sub_tasks.requirements: Fusion constraint has been implemented that forces fused operators to reuse a shared buffer at the fusion level L_fuse, with child nodes sharing the buffer respecting its dynamic storage level.

verification.spec: Construct a fused 2-op subgraph where op1 and op2 are fused at L_fuse. Verify the MINLP contains a constraint that both ops reference the same buffer id at level L_fuse (buffer reuse), and that child nodes' Place variables for that shared buffer are tied to a single dynamic storage-level decision.

sub_tasks.requirements: Memory-capacity constraint has been implemented that requires, at every storage level sl, the sum of BufferSize over buffers with Place selecting sl to not exceed the hardware capacity C_sl.

verification.spec: Set an artificially tiny capacity C_sl for some level (e.g., 1 byte) in a toy MINLP model with multiple buffers. Solve and verify the solver reports infeasibility or forces all buffers off that level. Then increase C_sl and confirm a feasible solution appears, demonstrating sum(Place*BufferSize) <= C_sl is enforced.

sub_tasks.requirements: Hardware capacity values C_sl per memory level are configurable inputs to the solver (not hardcoded to a single platform), allowing the compiler to be retargeted to different memory hierarchies.

verification.spec: Instantiate the parametric optimizer with two different sets of per-level capacity values C_sl (e.g., a laptop CPU profile and a server CPU profile) and confirm the solver accepts both without code modification, producing different solutions. Assert C_sl is passed via a config/argument rather than hardcoded.

sub_tasks.requirements: The objective function modeling execution time as max(T_comp, T_mem) with a linear-regression micro-kernel model is implemented.
A linear regression model µKernelTime that predicts micro-kernel execution time from tile shape parameters is implemented and used as the innermost compute-time estimator.

verification.spec: Locate the µKernelTime model class/function. Verify (a) it is a linear regression whose features are tile shape parameters, (b) it exposes a predict(tile_shape)->time API, and (c) predictions vary linearly when tile shapes are scaled. Fit on a small synthetic dataset and confirm coefficients are learned.

sub_tasks.requirements: The compute time T_comp is computed by scaling µKernelTime by the enclosing iteration/trip counts, matching the formulation in Section 3.2.2.

verification.spec: For a toy 2-level tile graph, evaluate T_comp and verify the expression equals µKernelTime(innermost_tile_shape) multiplied by the enclosing TripCount. Doubling an outer TileVar should double T_comp; doubling an inner shape should update via µKernelTime.

sub_tasks.requirements: The memory time T_mem is computed per level as data traffic at that level divided by that level's bandwidth BW_l, and summed/reduced across levels as in Section 3.2.2.

verification.spec: For a toy multi-level graph with known traffic per level, evaluate T_mem. Verify per-level term equals Traffic(l)/BW_l and that the aggregate matches the Section 3.2.2 formulation (sum or max over levels as coded). Change BW_l and confirm T_mem scales inversely.

sub_tasks.requirements: The final MINLP objective minimizes max(T_comp, T_mem), modeling the assumption of overlapped compute and memory execution.

verification.spec: Inspect the objective added to the MINLP solver and verify it is min(z) subject to z >= T_comp and z >= T_mem (i.e., z models max(T_comp, T_mem)). Solve two toy instances: one compute-bound (T_comp>>T_mem) and one memory-bound; confirm the optimal objective equals the larger of the two in each case.

sub_tasks.requirements: Per-level memory bandwidth BW_l values are configurable inputs consumed by the memory-time expression, enabling retargeting to different memory hierarchies.

verification.spec: Invoke the parametric optimizer twice with different BW_l dictionaries (e.g., DDR4 vs HBM profiles) passed as configuration. Verify the T_mem expression uses the provided BW_l values (assert distinct T_mem outputs for identical traffic under different BW configs). Confirm BW_l is not hardcoded.

sub_tasks.requirements: The MINLP problem is dispatched to a solver and integrated into the Auto Schedule pipeline as the parametric evaluator for MCTS structural search.
Code has been implemented that submits the assembled objective and constraints to Google OR-Tools (or equivalent MINLP-capable solver) and retrieves the tile-size and buffer-placement solution.

verification.spec: Import the parametric optimization module and verify it exposes a solver entrypoint (e.g., solve_tile_params) that constructs an OR-Tools MINLP/CP-SAT model, submits it, and returns a solution object containing tile-size and buffer-placement assignments. Confirm via source inspection or by running the solver on a trivial 1-op tile graph and checking the returned dict has 'tile_sizes' and 'buffer_placement' keys.

sub_tasks.requirements: The solver interface returns the estimated latency (objective value) for a given Tiered Tile Graph structure, which the MCTS Simulation phase consumes as its reward signal.

verification.spec: Construct a small Tiered Tile Graph fixture, invoke the parametric solver, and assert that it returns a numeric estimated latency (float) alongside the parametric solution. Then invoke the MCTS module's simulation/evaluation hook on the same leaf state and verify that the reward it consumes equals (or is a monotonic function of) the solver's returned latency.

sub_tasks.requirements: Given a fixed structural Tiered Tile Graph and hardware description, invoking the parametric solver twice yields the same optimal tile-size / buffer-placement solution (deterministic given fixed solver seed/settings).

verification.spec: Build a fixed Tiered Tile Graph and hardware descriptor, call the parametric solver twice with identical inputs and fixed seed, and assert that the returned tile-size vector and buffer-placement assignments are element-wise equal across the two runs.

sub_tasks.requirements: When the memory-capacity constraint at any level is set below the smallest feasible buffer size, the solver reports infeasibility rather than emitting a solution that violates capacity.

verification.spec: Construct a tile graph whose smallest feasible buffer footprint is B bytes. Invoke the solver with memory capacity C_sl = B-1 at some level sl. Assert the solver returns an infeasible/UNSAT status (e.g., raises SolverInfeasible or returns status != OPTIMAL/FEASIBLE) and does NOT return a solution assigning buffers to level sl exceeding C_sl.

sub_tasks.requirements: For a simple GEMM tile-graph test case, the solver selects a larger tile size when the L2 capacity is increased (all other parameters fixed), demonstrating that capacity feeds back into tile-size selection.

verification.spec: Build a GEMM-only tile graph. Solve twice: once with a small L2 capacity C1 and once with a larger L2 capacity C2 > C1 (all other parameters fixed). Assert that the product of tile sizes (or the tile volume) selected in the C2 run is strictly greater than in the C1 run.

sub_tasks.requirements: The buffer scheduling with alias analysis and SAT-based bin-packing memory planning is implemented as part of the code generation phase, translating the optimized computation graph into hardware-aware C++ source code with minimized memory redundancy and access overhead.
The bufferization stage that maps logical tensors to physical buffer constraints is implemented, including alias analysis for view-semantic operators.

Code has been implemented that provides a Bufferization pass converting logical tensors from the optimized computation graph into physical buffer objects with associated size, dtype, and storage-level metadata.

verification.spec: Feed a small optimized computation graph (e.g., MatMul + Add) through the Bufferization pass and inspect the output IR/data structure. Assert each logical tensor is mapped to a physical buffer object exposing 'size' (bytes), 'dtype', and 'storage_level' (or equivalent) attributes.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that performs Alias Analysis identifying view-semantic operators including Reshape, Slice, and Squeeze whose outputs are marked as aliases of their input physical buffers.

verification.spec: Construct a small graph containing Reshape, Slice, and Squeeze operators. Run the Alias Analysis pass and assert that the output buffer of each of these operators is flagged as an alias (e.g., is_alias=True) whose alias-source is the corresponding input buffer.

sub_tasks.requirements: For each identified alias relationship, the compiler must not emit a fresh allocation for the aliased output; the generated code path must reuse the underlying physical buffer of the source tensor (zero-copy execution for shape transformations).

verification.spec: Compile a graph containing a Reshape (and separately a Slice/Squeeze) and inspect the generated code or allocation table. Assert that no new buffer allocation is emitted for the view operator's output and that its data pointer/offset equals that of its input buffer (zero-copy).

sub_tasks.requirements: Alias analysis correctly propagates through chains of view operators (e.g., Reshape → Slice → Squeeze), so that all view descendants of a single source buffer resolve to the same underlying physical storage.

verification.spec: Build a chain X -> Reshape -> Slice -> Squeeze -> Y. Run alias analysis and assert that the physical buffer resolved for Y (and the two intermediates) is the same underlying storage object as X's buffer (identity/id equality on the resolved physical buffer).

sub_tasks.requirements: Liveness analysis over the computation graph produces the lifecycle (birth/death) and size of each non-aliased buffer needed for memory planning.
